name.full: Sorrel Vey from before the Tally

epithet: who knew the singing but not the dead
mannerisms: never sits with their back to a door
will not say a name they have not earned
keeps a list of people whose birthdays no one else remembers
voice: flat, deliberate, no music allowed in
aspiration: to build a temple their children will recognize
fear: being misunderstood after they are gone
wound: a decade given to the wrong thing
secret: that the founder they revere was a fraud

threads.desc: who became necessary to the work without either of them saying so
who said the right sentence at the right moment, and is unaware of any of it
whom {name} has been forgiving in installments for years

backstory.origin: Born in The Outer Ruins, from before the Tally, Sorrel grew up in a household where the kitchen was warm and the rest of the house was not.
backstory.weight: Their family carries no particular signature wound. What they inherited instead was a long, quiet expectation that one ought to be reasonable.
backstory.fracture: At nineteen, Sorrel entered a circle that was both deep and shared, and they have spent every year afterward trying to find another room of the same shape.
backstory.between: Between then and now, they did most of the ordinary things. They lived in a barge that never finished its route for a time, learned to mend their own clothes, and grew briefly close to a person whose name they will not say in mixed company.
backstory.present: These days, Sorrel can be found in the workshop most mornings. They have a small icon they did not buy that they will not throw away, and a habit of rereading the same page until they fall asleep that even their oldest friends find slightly strange.
